chunks.rationale: The bug. The old guard rejected removal if ANY thread in the project still carried a worktreePath. Measured against the live store: all 5 projects have such threads (74 total, 30 of them pointing at directories that no longer exist), so 'Remove project' could never succeed for a real project. The guard is replaced with reclaim via removeGcWorktree — the GC primitive, which never deletes a branch and uses a non-force `git worktree remove`, so uncommitted work cannot be destroyed. A failed reclaim warns and leaves the directory on disk rather than blocking. Function became async; the active-run guard still runs before any deletion so partial removal is still impossible.
risks: Orphaned directories: a dirty worktree survives the removal with no thread row pointing at it. gcScan's git-common-dir fallback still classifies it, so the GC panel can reclaim it later.
Sync -> async: every caller had to be awaited. Only electron/ipc.js and this test file call it (grepped).

chunks.rationale: removeGcWorktree was module-private; exported unchanged. ipc handler was already async, so only the await was missing.
risks: Missing the await would swallow the active-run rejection and report success to the renderer.

chunks.rationale: The catch discarded the real error, so every failure read 'Failed to remove "slug"' with no reason — which is why the cause stayed invisible for so long. Now appends err.message. State renamed removeFailSlug -> removeFailMessage since it no longer holds a slug.
risks: Two unrelated call sites (handleSetArchived, handleClearSettled) also cleared this state; a missed rename crashed 9 renderer tests at first and had to be fixed. Confirm no `removeFailSlug` remains.

chunks.rationale: Removal now deletes worktree folders, so the confirm dialog has to say so. Line only renders when the project actually has worktrees, and states what is kept (branches, repo) and what is skipped (dirty trees).
risks: worktreeCount is derived from the same `threads` prop as the existing thread count, so both share whatever filtering the sidebar applies.

chunks.rationale: The old suite asserted the guard that was the bug. Replaced with the three cases that matter: clean worktree reclaimed + branch kept, stale path does not block, dirty tree survives while the project still removes. assert.throws -> assert.rejects on the three guard tests now that the function is async.
risks: The dirty-worktree test is the data-loss canary; if a future change adds --force it fails.

Behaviour change on a destructive action: removing a project now deletes worktree directories it previously refused to touch. Mitigated by never deleting branches (every commit stays reachable), never force-removing, and saying so in the confirm dialog.

Verification: remove-project.test.js 10/10, full renderer suite 1338/1338, electron suite 1673 pass / 11 fail — all 11 in orch-server.test.js and identical on the stashed baseline, unrelated to this change.
